items.title: [Bug]: Profile `.env` does not clear inherited Hermes env vars (ACP/provider leak across gateways)

labels.name: sweeper:risk-compatibility
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may break existing users, config, migrations, defaults, or upgrades

items.body:
### Bug Description

Profiles are documented as fully isolated (`HERMES_HOME` + per-profile `.env`), but `load_hermes_dotenv()` only **sets/overrides** keys present in the profile `.env`. It does **not** unset Hermes-managed keys that exist in the parent process environment but are absent from the profile's `.env`.
When profile B's gateway is started/restarted from a process that already has profile A's Hermes env loaded, those keys leak into B and silently change **provider / ACP** behavior (not only messaging platforms).
`reload_env()` already removes known Hermes keys missing from `.env`, but startup (`load_hermes_dotenv`) does not — startup and hot-reload diverge.
Same isolation gap *class* as #68367 / #66930, but different vector/symptom:
- **Vector:** CLI / multi-gateway restart inheritance (Desktop spawn not required)
- **Symptom:** `copilot-acp` settings leak (`HERMES_ACP_AUTH_METHOD`, etc.) → ACP `authenticate` fails
- **Gap:** ACP keys are not in `OPTIONAL_ENV_VARS` / `_EXTRA_ENV_KEYS`, so even `reload_env()` would not clear them today
Related (please check vector before closing as duplicate):
- #68367 + PR #68786 — Desktop spawn scrub
- #66930 + PR #67027 — gateway Matrix / named-profile credential isolation
- #61046 + PR #61073 — root `.env` as base under profile `HERMES_HOME`

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Profile A (e.g. `all-rounder`) `.env` contains:

   HERMES_ACP_AUTH_METHOD=cursor_login

   (Cursor ACP)
2. Profile B (e.g. `coder`) `.env` does **not** define `HERMES_ACP_AUTH_METHOD`
   (Claude Code ACP via `@agentclientprotocol/claude-agent-acp`, `model.provider: copilot-acp`)
3. Restart profile B's gateway from a process that already has profile A's env loaded
   (e.g. consecutive multi-profile gateway restarts that inherit process env)
4. Send a Discord message to the profile B bot
5. Observe Discord: "The model provider failed after retries..."
6. Check gateway/agent logs for: `Copilot ACP authenticate failed: Internal error`

### Expected Behavior

Profile B runtime has no `HERMES_ACP_AUTH_METHOD` (or only values from its own `.env`).
Claude Code ACP advertises `authMethods: []` and must skip `authenticate`. The request should succeed(`initialize` → `session/new` → `session/prompt`).

### Actual Behavior

Coder profile inherits `HERMES_ACP_AUTH_METHOD=cursor_login` from another profile's process env, calls ACP `authenticate`, and fails. Discord then shows the redacted provider-failure message.
From `profiles/coder` logs (2026-07-30 15:18 KST), after a Discord message `테스트`:

API call failed (attempt 1/3) ... provider=copilot-acp ... Copilot ACP authenticate failed: Internal error
API call failed (attempt 2/3) ... Copilot ACP authenticate failed: Internal error
API call failed (attempt 3/3) ... Copilot ACP authenticate failed: Internal error
API call failed after 3 retries. Copilot ACP authenticate failed: Internal error | provider=copilot-acp model=auto msgs=2 tokens=~8,212

Direct probe of the Claude ACP server confirms:
`authenticate` → Internal error / Method not implemented (`authMethods: []`).

### Affected Component

Configuration (config.yaml, .env, hermes setup)

### Messaging Platform (if gateway-related)

Discord

### Debug Report

```shell
Report       https://paste.rs/4A4B4
agent.log    https://dpaste.com/7JNFWLMZ6
gateway.log  https://dpaste.com/5M4T9TVSY
```

### Operating System

Windows 11 Pro (10.0.26200)

### Python Version

3.11.15

### Hermes Version

0.19.0

### Additional Logs / Traceback (optional)

```shell
Note: `hermes debug share` was run from the default profile, so those pastes do not contain this failure. The failure is in the **coder** profile logs:
`~/.hermes/profiles/coder/logs/agent.log` / `errors.log`

2026-07-30 15:18:37,470 INFO gateway.run: inbound message: platform=discord user=world chat=1532271171444146217 msg='테스트' ...
2026-07-30 15:18:40,147 INFO run_agent: Copilot ACP client created (agent_init, ...) provider=copilot-acp base_url=acp://copilot model=auto
2026-07-30 15:18:43,186 INFO [20260730_151837_09412673] agent.turn_context: conversation turn: session=20260730_151837_09412673 model=auto provider=copilot-acp platform=discord ...
2026-07-30 15:18:44,090 WARNING [20260730_151837_09412673] agent.conversation_loop: API call failed (attempt 1/3) error_type=RuntimeError thread=hermes-gateway_0:28624 provider=copilot-acp base_url=acp://copilot model=auto summary=Copilot ACP authenticate failed: Internal error
2026-07-30 15:18:44,092 WARNING [20260730_151837_09412673] agent.conversation_loop: Retrying API call in 2.54s (attempt 1/3) ... error=Copilot ACP authenticate failed: Internal error
2026-07-30 15:18:47,065 WARNING [20260730_151837_09412673] agent.conversation_loop: API call failed (attempt 2/3) ... summary=Copilot ACP authenticate failed: Internal error
2026-07-30 15:18:47,066 WARNING [20260730_151837_09412673] agent.conversation_loop: Retrying API call in 4.46s (attempt 2/3) ...
2026-07-30 15:18:52,045 WARNING [20260730_151837_09412673] agent.conversation_loop: API call failed (attempt 3/3) ... summary=Copilot ACP authenticate failed: Internal error
2026-07-30 15:18:52,074 ERROR [20260730_151837_09412673] agent.conversation_loop: API call failed after 3 retries. Copilot ACP authenticate failed: Internal error | provider=copilot-acp model=auto msgs=2 tokens=~8,212
2026-07-30 15:18:52,600 WARNING agent.title_generator: Title generation failed: Copilot ACP authenticate failed: Internal error
2026-07-30 15:18:52,235 INFO gateway.run: response ready: platform=discord chat=1532271171444146217 time=14.8s api_calls=1 response=80 chars

Discord user-visible reply (redacted by Hermes):
> The model provider failed after retries. I kept raw provider details out of chat; check gateway logs for diagnostics.
Independent ACP probe against `@agentclientprotocol/claude-agent-acp` (the coder profile backend):
- `authenticate` with `methodId=cursor_login` →
  `{"error":{"code":-32603,"message":"Internal error","data":{"details":"Method not implemented."}}}`
  (server advertises `authMethods: []`)
- Without `authenticate` → `session/prompt` succeeds normally
After setting `HERMES_ACP_AUTH_METHOD=` in the coder profile `.env` and restarting that gateway, Discord turns succeed again (e.g. 16:20 session completed without authenticate errors).
```

### Root Cause Analysis (optional)

Process inheritance is normal. The bug is Hermes advertises per-profile `.env` isolation, and already implements the correct unset semantics in `reload_env()`, but not on initial load:
- `hermes_cli/env_loader.py` → `load_hermes_dotenv()` — override only
- `hermes_cli/config.py` → `reload_env()` — override **and** delete known keys missing from `.env`
Also `HERMES_ACP_AUTH_METHOD` / `HERMES_COPILOT_ACP_*` are missing from `_EXTRA_ENV_KEYS`, so known-key cleanup cannot see them.

### Proposed Fix (optional)

 1. After loading the profile `.env` in `load_hermes_dotenv()`, mirror `reload_env()`: for each known Hermes key not present in that `.env`, `del os.environ[key]`.
2. Add ACP-related keys to `_EXTRA_ENV_KEYS` (`HERMES_ACP_AUTH_METHOD`, `HERMES_ACP_AUTO_APPROVE`, `HERMES_COPILOT_ACP_COMMAND`, `HERMES_COPILOT_ACP_ARGS`, `COPILOT_CLI_PATH`, `COPILOT_ACP_BASE_URL`).
3. Do not clear when no `.env` exists (bare-profile / #66930 semantics).
4. Preserve explicit empty `KEY=` assignments.
I have a branch ready on my fork:
https://github.com/keepConcentration/hermes-agent/tree/fix/profile-env-clear-inherited-known-keys

items.body:
## Bug: Hermes gateway streaming receives 0 chunks from custom provider (CPA/OpenAI-compatible endpoint)

### Environment
- Hermes Agent v0.19.1 (2026.7.30)
- OS: Oracle Linux (ARM64)
- Custom provider: CPA (CLI-Proxy-API) / OpenAI-compatible endpoint using Antigravity credentials

### Description

When using Hermes gateway with a custom provider pointing to a CPA/OpenAI-compatible endpoint, streaming calls to `chat/completions` fail to receive any data chunks, resulting in a **"stream stale timeout" (0 chunks received)**.

The backend (CPA) logs confirm a successful `200 OK` response is sent, but Hermes reports receiving 0 chunks.

### Confirmed facts

- ✅ `curl` from the same machine → works
- ✅ Python `openai` SDK from the same machine → works
- ✅ Codex CLI from the same machine → works
- ❌ Hermes gateway process → **fails** (stream stale timeout, 0 chunks received)

### What has been ruled out

- **Request body size**: Disabling `tools` in the request didn't help
- **Hermes version**: Rolling back to v0.17.0 didn't help
- **Nginx**: Connecting directly via IP:port (bypassing Nginx) also fails

### Core question

How does Hermes gateway's streaming reception implementation differ from standard OpenAI SDK calls? The same endpoint works perfectly with every other client, so the issue appears to be specific to how Hermes handles incoming SSE/streaming chunks from custom providers.

### Expected behavior

Hermes gateway should receive streaming chunks from a custom OpenAI-compatible provider that returns a valid `200 OK` streaming response.

### Actual behavior

Hermes gateway reports 0 chunks received and times out with "stream stale timeout", even though the backend confirms sending a successful 200 streaming response.

labels.name: comp/cli
labels.description: CLI entry point, hermes_cli/, setup wizard

labels.name: sweeper:risk-compatibility
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may break existing users, config, migrations, defaults, or upgrades

items.body:
# Draft GitHub issue — NousResearch/hermes-agent

## Proposed title

`[Bug]: WSL managed update leaves SQLite 3.50.4 while warning says hermes update can repair it; existing WAL DBs lack guided remediation`

## Summary

A git-installed Hermes Agent on Ubuntu 24.04 under WSL2 was successfully updated on 2026-07-30, but the active uv-managed Python runtime still embeds SQLite 3.50.4. Hermes continues to warn that the runtime is vulnerable to the WAL-reset bug and says that `hermes update` can repair it.

The update did not replace the runtime, and existing databases already in WAL mode remained in WAL because Hermes correctly refuses to live-downgrade them while concurrent processes may have them open. This leaves users with a warning that points to an update path that does not complete the repair and no supported guided workflow for safely converting existing databases.

This is related to #69784 and #71250, but this report focuses on the still-reproducible WSL managed-runtime/update and existing-WAL remediation gap.

## Environment

- OS: Ubuntu 24.04 under WSL2
- Hermes install: git-managed
- Hermes reported version after today's update: v0.19.0 (2026.7.20)
- A later v0.19.1 update became available the same day; repository was 30 commits behind when checked
- Python: uv-managed CPython 3.11.15
- SQLite runtime: 3.50.4
- Main database stored on WSL ext4, not `/mnt/c` or `/mnt/d`
- Gateway and dashboard run as separate user-systemd processes

## Steps to reproduce

1. Install/update Hermes using its supported managed update path.
2. Verify Hermes and SQLite versions:

   ```bash
   hermes version
   python -c 'import sqlite3; print(sqlite3.sqlite_version)'
   ```

3. Observe that Hermes is updated but SQLite remains 3.50.4.
4. Start Hermes with existing databases that are already in WAL mode.
5. Observe warnings similar to:

   ```text
   linked SQLite 3.50.4 is vulnerable to the WAL-reset corruption bug
   — is already in WAL mode — leaving WAL in place (no live downgrade
   under concurrent openers). Upgrade to SQLite 3.51.3+ (or backports
   3.50.7 / 3.44.6); Hermes-managed installs can repair the embedded
   runtime with `hermes update`.
   ```

6. Run `hermes update` and re-check `sqlite3.sqlite_version`.

## Actual behavior

- The update can complete while the managed Python still embeds SQLite 3.50.4.
- The warning continues to tell the user that `hermes update` can repair the embedded runtime.
- Existing WAL databases remain in WAL for valid safety reasons.
- There is no supported guided command that safely:
  - drains/stops Hermes processes;
  - snapshots and integrity-checks the database;
  - checkpoints the WAL;
  - changes the database to DELETE mode;
  - restarts and verifies the gateway.

In this incident, the gateway later logged a failed session write:

```text
Session DB append_message failed: ... returned NULL without setting an exception
```

It had also logged persisted transcripts lagging behind live cached history and earlier `database is locked` events. `PRAGMA quick_check` still returned `ok`, so this is evidence of a write/persistence failure, not a claim of proven physical corruption from the WAL-reset bug.

Manual recovery required stopping the gateway, creating an integrity-checked local snapshot, changing `state.db` to DELETE mode while no process had it open, and restarting/verifying the gateway.

## Expected behavior

At least one of the following should be true:

1. `hermes update` installs a managed Python runtime containing a fixed SQLite version; or
2. The warning clearly states that the current update cannot repair this installation and gives a supported next step; and
3. Hermes provides a safe guided maintenance command for existing WAL databases on vulnerable runtimes.

The command should use local Linux storage for SQLite snapshots and should not construct a large SQLite backup directly under `/mnt/c` or `/mnt/d`.

## Suggested improvements

- Make the warning conditional on whether the updater can actually provision a fixed runtime for the current platform/Python line.
- After `hermes update`, verify and print the resulting SQLite version rather than implying repair from a successful Hermes update alone.
- Add a supported command such as `hermes doctor --repair-sqlite-runtime` or `hermes sessions migrate-journal-mode --safe` that performs stopped-state snapshot, integrity, journal conversion, restart, and verification.
- Detect existing WAL databases across `state.db`, Kanban boards, memory, verification evidence, and cron stores, then report which remain exposed.
- Ensure health checks discover the configured dashboard port instead of hardcoding one.

## Safety and privacy notes

- No database files, credentials, user messages, or private paths are attached.
- The live database passed `PRAGMA quick_check = ok` after the incident.
- This report does not claim that the WAL-reset bug was definitively the cause of the observed failed write; it reports the unresolved vulnerable-runtime and remediation gap.

## Related issues

- #69784 — bundled SQLite 3.50.4 WAL-reset corruption report
- #71250 — managed runtime repair failure on macOS
- #72093 — stale WAL-reset warning/dead-end provisioning
- #57820 — configurable DELETE journal mode

items.title: [Bug]: /steer fallback overwrites the existing gateway FIFO head

labels.name: sweeper:risk-message-delivery
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may drop, duplicate, misroute, or suppress messages

items.body:
### Bug Description

When a busy gateway `/steer` cannot be delivered to a live agent, the command reports that it was queued for the next turn. However, both fallback branches replace `adapter._pending_messages[session_key]` directly.

That dictionary entry is the head of the gateway FIFO. If earlier follow-ups are already queued, the direct assignment permanently loses the current head and places the newer steer ahead of the existing overflow.

This affects both fallback states:

- the running-turn slot still contains `_AGENT_PENDING_SENTINEL`; and
- the running agent is missing `steer()`.

### Steps to Reproduce

A deterministic non-network reproduction on current `main`:

1. Queue `Q1` and `Q2` for one gateway session through the existing FIFO helper.
   - `Q1` is stored in `adapter._pending_messages[session_key]`.
   - `Q2` is stored in `SessionState.conversation.queued_events`.
2. Set the session's running agent to `_AGENT_PENDING_SENTINEL` (the same result occurs with an agent object that lacks `steer()`).
3. Dispatch `/steer Q3` for the same session.
4. Inspect or drain the pending FIFO.

Observed state transition:

```text
before = ['Q1', 'Q2']
command result = Agent still starting — /steer queued for the next turn.
after = ['Q3', 'Q2']
```

### Expected Behavior

All accepted follow-ups survive and execute in arrival order:

```text
Q1, Q2, Q3
```

### Actual Behavior

`Q1` is permanently lost and the newer steer runs before `Q2`:

```text
Q3, Q2
```

The user receives a successful queue acknowledgement even though an earlier accepted message was discarded.

### Affected Component

Gateway runner / busy command dispatch.

### Messaging Platform (if gateway-related)

The reproduction uses a Telegram `SessionSource`, but the bug is in the shared gateway runner and applies to adapters using the shared pending-message FIFO.

### Debug Report

```shell
Hermes Agent v0.19.1
main: cc4cab2f592e60a197e796506de9168f74baf3ea
Python: 3.11.15
OS: Linux / WSL2
```

### Root Cause Analysis

`GatewayRunner._enqueue_fifo()` defines the queue contract: the adapter pending slot is the FIFO head and `SessionState.conversation.queued_events` is the overflow tail (`gateway/run.py:7312-7335`).

`GatewayRunner._busy_steer_command()` bypasses that contract in both fallback branches:

```python
adapter._pending_messages[quick_key] = queued_event
```

Current locations are `gateway/run.py:13511` and `gateway/run.py:13534`. Because the assignment does not preserve or requeue the existing head, `Q1` has no remaining reference after `/steer Q3`.

The existing fallback test starts with an empty pending queue, so it verifies only that `Q3` is stored and cannot detect this overwrite (`tests/gateway/test_steer_command.py:119-143`).

This is distinct from #72674, which restores FIFO state at the recursion-depth boundary but does not change `_busy_steer_command()`.

### Proposed Fix

Route both `/steer` fallback branches through the existing FIFO enqueue contract instead of assigning the pending slot directly. Add regression coverage for both `_AGENT_PENDING_SENTINEL` and an agent lacking `steer()` with `Q1`/`Q2` prequeued, asserting that the resulting order remains `Q1`, `Q2`, `Q3` and no event is lost.

### Are you willing to submit a PR for this?

- [x] I'd like to fix this myself and submit a PR

items.body:
### Bug Description

After switching/re-selecting the main model in the **desktop app** (Settings → Model, or the model picker during onboarding), `model.api_key` and `model.base_url` in `config.yaml` are silently cleared to empty strings (`''`). The desktop status bar then shows "model not connected" and "refresh models" has no effect — every provider that relies on a custom `base_url` or a non-default `api_key` (e.g. Xiaomi MiMo Token Plan, SiliconFlow custom endpoints) becomes unusable until the user manually restores the values.

The config file on disk was found with:
```yaml
model:
  api_key: ''
  base_url: ''
  default: mimo-v2.5-pro
  provider: xiaomi
```
while `.env` still contained `XIAOMI_API_KEY` and `XIAOMI_BASE_URL` — so the environment was fine; the config-level empty strings shadow the env vars.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Configure any provider whose endpoint needs a custom `base_url` + `api_key` (e.g. Xiaomi MiMo Token Plan: `https://token-plan-cn.xiaomimimo.com/v1`) in `config.yaml`:
   ```yaml
   model:
     provider: xiaomi
     default: mimo-v2.5-pro
     base_url: ${XIAOMI_BASE_URL}
     api_key: ${XIAOMI_API_KEY}
   ```
2. Open the desktop app → Settings → Model (or complete onboarding), pick the same provider/model again and save.
3. Check `config.yaml` → `model.api_key` and `model.base_url` are now `''`.
4. Desktop status bar shows "model not connected"; refreshing models does nothing.

### Expected Behavior

Re-selecting a model under the **same provider** must preserve the existing `model.api_key` / `model.base_url` (the backend `_apply_main_model_assignment` already has this intent — see `hermes_cli/web_server.py` — but the frontend never sends the key/URL, so the wipe path triggers).

### Actual Behavior

The desktop frontend calls `POST /api/model/set` with only `{scope, provider, model}` — `api_key` and `base_url` are omitted:

```typescript
// apps/desktop/src/app/settings/model-settings.tsx (applyMainModel)
const result = await setModelAssignment({
  model: selectedModel,
  provider: selectedProvider,
  scope: 'main',
  ...(selectedProviderRow?.api_url ? { base_url: selectedProviderRow.api_url } : {})
  // api_key never sent
})
```

The backend `_apply_main_model_assignment` (`hermes_cli/web_server.py`) then wipes existing credentials:

```python
if api_key.strip():
    model_cfg["api_key"] = api_key.strip()
elif (model_cfg.get("api_key") or model_cfg.get("api")) and new_provider != prev_provider:
    clear_model_endpoint_credentials(model_cfg, clear_api_mode=False)
```

Note: even a **same-provider re-pick** wipes the key when the frontend omits `api_key` and the stored key is under `model.api` or when `base_url` is dropped — in our case the wipe happened on a same-provider re-selection and both fields ended up `''`.

Impact: any user with a custom endpoint loses connectivity after a GUI model switch. Workaround: restore the values manually in `config.yaml` (or use `${ENV_VAR}` references, which survive only if the config strings aren't wiped).

### Environment
- OS: Windows 10
- Version: latest `hermes update` (2.x, commit a2a74d7ac)
- Desktop app, provider: xiaomi (MiMo Token Plan custom endpoint)

### Root Cause Analysis

Two layers combine:
1. **Frontend** (`apps/desktop/src/app/settings/model-settings.tsx`, and onboarding `apps/desktop/src/store/onboarding.ts` → `completeWithModelConfirm`) never sends `api_key` (and only sometimes `base_url`) in `setModelAssignment`.
2. **Backend** (`hermes_cli/web_server.py::_apply_main_model_assignment`) treats an omitted field as "clear it" whenever the provider changed — and for `base_url` the same-provider branch can also clear it. There is no "not provided" vs "explicitly empty" distinction because the endpoint signature defaults both to `""`.

### Proposed Fix

- Backend: distinguish "field absent" from "field empty" in `POST /api/model/set` (e.g. use `None` default / optional fields) so an omitted `api_key`/`base_url` preserves the existing config value; only clear on an explicit provider switch with explicit empty values.
- Frontend: include the resolved provider row's `api_key`/`base_url` in `setModelAssignment` payload (or omit them and rely on the backend preserve-when-absent behavior).

items.title: Credential pool rotates to the single pool entry instead of stopping when the failed key matches no pool entry

labels.name: comp/agent
labels.description: Core agent runtime: loop, agent_init, prompt builder, context-compression, responses endpoint

items.body:
## Bug Description

When a credential pool contains exactly **one** entry and the agent's failing credential **matches no pool entry**, a 401 (non-entitlement) causes `recover_with_credential_pool()` to return `recovered = True` and rotate to that single entry — even though there is no *different* credential to rotate to. The test-suite contract for this case (`test_unmatched_key_does_not_retry_only_pool_entry`) expects recovery to **stop** (`recovered is False`). The implementation and the test disagree, and the implementation currently wins.

This matters because rotating to the same effective credential under a fresh label produces a redundant retry of an already-failed auth situation, and (per the test's encoded contract) violates the intended "stop when there is nothing different to rotate to" behavior for legacy agents without a stable id.

This is a deterministic test failure on a clean, unmodified upstream checkout — not caused by any local change.

## Affected revision

- Release: **v0.19.1** (`cc4cab2f592e60a197e796506de9168f74baf3ea`)
- Current `main` at time of report: **`b1858f33a1cc6083ee34aea41417ea5e18564d2e`** — failure reproduced on both.

## Environment

- OS: Ubuntu 24.04.4 LTS (kernel 7.0.0-28-generic)
- Python: 3.11.15 (the project's `.venv` interpreter)
- pytest: 9.0.2
- Install method: git checkout

## Steps to Reproduce

```bash
git clone https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent.git
cd hermes-agent
git checkout b1858f33a1cc6083ee34aea41417ea5e18564d2e   # or v0.19.1 / cc4cab2f5

# create the project venv and install test deps per CONTRIBUTING, then:
python -m pytest \
  tests/agent/test_credential_pool_routing.py::TestFailureAttribution::test_unmatched_key_does_not_retry_only_pool_entry \
  -q
```

## Expected Behavior

Per the test's docstring ("Legacy agents without a stable id must stop when an unmatched key has no different credential to rotate to"):

- `recover_with_credential_pool(agent, status_code=401, has_retried_429=False)` returns `recovered is False`
- `agent._swap_credential` is **not** called

## Actual Behavior

`recovered is True` — the pool rotates to the single entry `cred-0` anyway.

```
>       assert recovered is False
E       assert True is False

tests/agent/test_credential_pool_routing.py:491: AssertionError
```

## Reproducibility

- Runs: 3 consecutive runs on pristine v0.19.1 + 1 run on current `main` (b1858f33a), plus runs on a tree with unrelated local commits.
- Outcome: **fails identically on every run** (same assertion, same line 491).
- Diagnostic logging: with INFO-level logging enabled (`--log-cli-level=INFO`), the following two lines are emitted on **every** run, on both pristine and working trees:

```
INFO agent.credential_pool:credential_pool.py:1855 credential pool: failed credential identity matched no anthropic entry; rotating without marking any credential exhausted
INFO run_agent:agent_runtime_helpers.py:1221 Credential 401 (auth refresh failed) — rotated to pool entry cred-0
```

Note: these INFO lines only appear when INFO-level log capture is explicitly enabled; they are not part of the default `-q` failure output. The **behavioral** failure (`assert True is False`) is fully deterministic regardless of logging configuration.

## Clean-upstream confirmation

Reproduced on a `git worktree` checked out at `cc4cab2f5` (v0.19.1) with **no local modifications**, and again on a pristine worktree at current `main` `b1858f33a`. No local patch touches `agent/credential_pool.py` or `agent/agent_runtime_helpers.py`. The failure is isolated: the other 14 tests in `test_credential_pool_routing.py` pass (1 failed, 14 passed).

## Scope

- Tested: the single-entry / unmatched-key / 401 path above, on Linux, Python 3.11.
- Not tested: multi-entry pools, other providers, other status codes, Windows/macOS.

## Additional notes

No proposed fix — root cause not proven. The open question for maintainers: when the failed credential's identity matches no pool entry **and** the pool has only one entry, should rotation be treated as recovery (current implementation behavior) or as a stop condition (the test's encoded expectation)? The test name and docstring indicate "stop" is the intended contract, which points to the implementation (`credential_pool.py` unmatched-identity rotation path) as the likely defect site — but that is a behavioral-contract observation, not a proven root cause.

(Debug Report field: a `hermes debug share` bundle is not materially relevant here — this is a deterministic, self-contained `pytest` failure on a pristine checkout with no gateway/session state involved. Happy to run `hermes debug share --local` and attach it if maintainers want the environment snapshot.)

items.body:
# models.dev unreachable from China blocks desktop model picker for 15s

## Problem

The desktop app's model picker shows skeleton loading bars for **15+ seconds** on every cold start in mainland China (and likely other regions where `models.dev` is unreachable).

### Root Cause

`models.dev` (108.160.172.232) is a third-party community database (not Hermes-owned). When it's unreachable:

1. The disk cache TTL is 1 hour (`_MODELS_DEV_CACHE_TTL = 3600`)
2. When the cache is stale (>1h), Stage 2 is skipped
3. Stage 3 fires a network request with a **15-second timeout**
4. After 15s timeout, Stage 4 falls back to the stale disk cache

So every cold start where the disk cache is >1h old blocks for 15 seconds on a domain that can never be reached from this network.

### Reproduction

```bash
# Direct connection fails (timeout after 15s):
curl --connect-timeout 5 https://models.dev/api.json

# Other Hermes dependencies work fine:
curl --connect-timeout 5 https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs/api/model-catalog.json  # OK
curl --connect-timeout 5 https://openrouter.ai/api/v1/models  # OK
```

### Comparison with model-catalog.json

The Nous Portal `model-catalog.json` handles this correctly:
- Ships a bundled copy in the repo (`website/static/api/model-catalog.json`)
- Has `seed_cache_from_checkout()` that copies it to disk cache during `hermes update`
- Has GitHub raw fallback URL

`models.dev` has **none of these** offline safeguards.

## Proposed Fix (3 lines in `agent/models_dev.py`)

1. **Add `_MODELS_DEV_DISK_GRACE = 604800` (7 days)** — serve disk cache up to 7 days old without network attempt. models.dev is a third-party DB; new models appear infrequently (when providers add them), so 7-day staleness is acceptable.

2. **Stage 2 condition**: `disk_age < _MODELS_DEV_DISK_GRACE` (was `_MODELS_DEV_CACHE_TTL` = 1h)

3. **Network timeout**: 15s → **3s** — fast failure when unreachable. Still allows refresh when network IS available.

### Performance Impact

| Scenario | Before | After |
|----------|--------|-------|
| Cold start (cache >1h, blocked) | **15s timeout** | **0.03s** (disk cache hit) |
| Cold start (cache >7d, blocked) | **15s timeout** | **3s timeout → disk cache** |
| Network available | 1h TTL, then 15s fetch | 1h TTL, then 3s fetch |

### Diff

```diff
@@ -33,6 +33,10 @@
 MODELS_DEV_URL = "https://models.dev/api.json"
 _MODELS_DEV_CACHE_TTL = 3600  # 1 hour in-memory
+_MODELS_DEV_DISK_GRACE = 604800  # 7 days — serve stale disk cache when
+    # models.dev is unreachable (e.g. GFW-blocked). Third-party community
+    # DB; new models only appear when providers add them, so 7-day
+    # staleness is acceptable. When reachable, Stage 3 refreshes.

@@ -275,7 +279,7 @@
-        if disk_age is not None and disk_age < _MODELS_DEV_CACHE_TTL:
+        if disk_age is not None and disk_age < _MODELS_DEV_DISK_GRACE:

@@ -290,7 +294,7 @@
-        response = requests.get(MODELS_DEV_URL, timeout=15)
+        response = requests.get(MODELS_DEV_URL, timeout=3)
```

### Environment

- Windows 11 LTSC 2024, Hermes v3.x, main branch
- Mainland China (Shenzhen Unicom) — `models.dev` IP 108.160.172.232 unreachable
- Desktop app (Electron) model picker affected

### Labels

`bug`, `desktop`, `model-picker`, `offline`

items.title: [Bug]: auth: a transient read failure (EMFILE/EACCES) is classified as corruption and returns an empty store — one save away from wiping all credentials

labels.name: comp/cli
labels.description: CLI entry point, hermes_cli/, setup wizard

labels.name: P1
labels.description: High — major feature broken, no workaround

labels.name: sweeper:risk-security-boundary
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may affect sandboxing, auth, credentials, or sensitive data

items.body:
## Bug description

`_load_auth_store()` treats *any* exception from reading `auth.json` as corruption and returns an empty store. Transient OS-level read failures — `EMFILE` under fd exhaustion, `EACCES`, `EIO`, a stalled network mount — are not corruption, and the empty store it returns is one `_save_auth_store()` away from destroying every stored credential.

```python
# hermes_cli/auth.py:1120
def _load_auth_store(auth_file: Optional[Path] = None) -> Dict[str, Any]:
    auth_file = auth_file or _auth_file_path()
    if not auth_file.exists():
        return {"version": AUTH_STORE_VERSION, "providers": {}}

    try:
        raw = json.loads(auth_file.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    except Exception as exc:                      # <-- catches OSError(EMFILE) too
        corrupt_path = auth_file.with_suffix(".json.corrupt")
        try:
            import shutil
            shutil.copy2(auth_file, corrupt_path)
        except Exception:
            pass                                  # <-- also fails under EMFILE, silently
        logger.warning(
            "auth: failed to parse %s (%s) — starting with empty store. "
            "Corrupt file preserved at %s",
            auth_file, exc, corrupt_path,
        )
        return {"version": AUTH_STORE_VERSION, "providers": {}}
```

Two things make this destructive rather than merely noisy:

**1. This module does read-modify-write.** There are ~15 `_load_auth_store()` → mutate → `_save_auth_store()` pairs (e.g. lines 736→743, 1256→1317, 1375→1378, 1783→1812, 2580→2585, 3032→3049). A load that silently degrades to `{"version": …, "providers": {}}` followed by any save rewrites `auth.json` with an empty provider set. An OAuth token refresh landing in that window is enough.

**2. The safety net does not arm.** The `shutil.copy2` backup opens a file — so under `EMFILE` it fails too, and its bare `except: pass` swallows that. The log line still claims `Corrupt file preserved at …` when nothing was preserved.

## How it was hit

Observed on a dashboard process that had exhausted its fds through an unrelated `SessionDB` connection leak (that leak is #72782; the 256-fd ceiling that set the deadline is #36899). While fds were exhausted, this fired every ~2 seconds:

```text
2026-07-30 20:11:19,087 WARNING hermes_cli.auth: auth: failed to parse ~/.hermes/auth.json
  ([Errno 24] Too many open files: '~/.hermes/auth.json') — starting with empty store.
  Corrupt file preserved at ~/.hermes/auth.json.corrupt
2026-07-30 20:11:19,088 WARNING hermes_cli.auth: auth: failed to parse ~/.hermes/auth.json ...
2026-07-30 20:11:19,089 WARNING hermes_cli.auth: auth: failed to parse ~/.hermes/auth.json ...
```

No `auth.json.corrupt` was ever created, confirming the backup path was failing too. The store survived only because no `_save_auth_store()` happened to land in that window — 3 providers plus the credential pool were still intact when the process was restarted. That is luck, not a safeguard.

This is worth fixing independently of the two fd issues: any cause of a transient read failure reaches it, and fd exhaustion is only the one that made it fire continuously.

## Reproduction

```python
import errno, json, tempfile
from pathlib import Path
from unittest import mock
import hermes_cli.auth as auth

d = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp()); f = d / "auth.json"
f.write_text(json.dumps({"version": 1, "providers": {"nous": {"k": "v"}}}))

with mock.patch.object(Path, "read_text",
                       side_effect=OSError(errno.EMFILE, "Too many open files")):
    store = auth._load_auth_store(f)

print(store)                                  # {'version': 1, 'providers': {}}  <-- credentials gone
print((d / "auth.json.corrupt").exists())     # False — the "preserved" copy was never written
```

Any subsequent `_save_auth_store(store)` persists that empty dict over the real file.

## Expected behavior

- A file that exists but cannot be **read** raises, rather than degrading to an empty store. The caller gets a real error naming the real cause and the file on disk is left untouched.
- Only a genuine parse failure (`json.JSONDecodeError`) takes the preserve-and-start-empty branch.
- The "Corrupt file preserved at …" message is only emitted when a copy was actually made.

## Proposed minimal fix

Add an `except OSError: raise` arm ahead of the catch-all:

```python
    try:
        raw = json.loads(auth_file.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    except OSError:
        # The file is there (we just checked) but could not be READ — EMFILE,
        # EACCES, EIO, a stalled mount. That is not corruption, and the empty
        # store this would otherwise return is one _save_auth_store() away from
        # destroying every stored credential.
        logger.warning(
            "auth: could not read %s — leaving the store on disk untouched "
            "rather than degrading to an empty one", auth_file, exc_info=True,
        )
        raise
    except Exception as exc:
        ...  # unchanged: genuine corruption still preserves a copy and degrades
```

Verified locally:

- `OSError(EMFILE)` propagates; `auth.json` unmodified; no `.corrupt` sidecar written
- malformed JSON still degrades to an empty store and still preserves a copy (unchanged)
- healthy loads unaffected
- `tests/hermes_cli` shows zero new failures against a pristine `git archive HEAD` baseline

Worth pairing with a regression test asserting that a read error propagates while a parse error does not, and separately tightening the log line so it cannot claim a copy that `copy2` failed to write.

## Environment

- macOS 25.5.0, Python 3.11.15
- hermes-agent v0.19.0 @ `b1858f33a1cc6083ee34aea41417ea5e18564d2e`
- Reached via fd exhaustion in the dashboard process (`hermes dashboard`, in-process `tui_gateway`)

### Bug Description

Environment
OS: Windows 10/11 [PLEASE FILL IN: exact build — run winver or [System.Environment]::OSVersion.Version]
Hermes Agent version: [PLEASE FILL IN: output of hermes --version]
Hermes Desktop version: [PLEASE FILL IN: Settings → About in the app]
Install method: native Windows PowerShell installer (irm https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/install.ps1 | iex)
Updater binary involved: %LOCALAPPDATA%\hermes\hermes-setup.exe
Description

Clicking Update in Hermes Desktop on Windows always fails with:

UPDATE DIDN'T FINISH Hermes is still running. Close all Hermes windows and try the update again.

This happens even with zero other Hermes-related processes running, no system-tray icon, and no stale lock files present. The failure reproduces on every retry, each time with a freshly spawned PID, and the log shows the updater detecting itself as the conflicting "already running" instance — the reported PID and "started Ns ago" delta match the updater's own process exactly.

### Steps to Reproduce

Steps to Reproduce
Install Hermes natively on Windows via the documented PowerShell installer.
Open Hermes Desktop, let it boot normally (confirmed working).
Click Update (or Retry update) in the app.
Observe the "UPDATE DIDN'T FINISH" screen.
Confirm no other Hermes processes are running:
powershell
   Get-Process | Where-Object { $_.Path -like "*hermes*" -or $_.ProcessName -like "*hermes*" -or $_.ProcessName -like "*electron*" }

→ only the updater's own hermes-setup.exe process is listed (the one that just started). 6. Confirm no stale lock: %LOCALAPPDATA%\hermes\hermes-agent\venv\.lock does not exist (verified deleted / absent between attempts). 7. Click Retry again — same failure occurs, with a new PID.

### Expected Behavior

Expected Behavior

The "wait for Hermes to exit / check for a concurrent update" step should exclude the updater's own PID from its "is another instance already running" check, and the update should proceed normally when no other Hermes process is actually present.

Hypothesis

The check that produces "Another Hermes update is already running (PID …)" appears to enumerate running processes by name (e.g. a wildcard/prefix match such as hermes* or hermes-setup*) rather than checking a PID-ownership lock file that is written before the check and correctly skips GetCurrentProcessId(). Because hermes-setup.exe itself matches that name pattern, every fresh run detects itself as "another" instance, with the reported "started Ns ago" always equal to its own uptime. This reproduced identically across two separate runs with two different (freshly-assigned) PIDs, ruling out a stale/leftover process or lock file as the cause — both were ruled out and retried clean:

No other hermes/electron process running at time of retry (Get-Process empty except the new updater itself).
No system tray icon.
%LOCALAPPDATA%\hermes\hermes-agent\venv\.lock absent both before and after the failed attempt.
Workaround (confirmed working)

Since the in-app updater cannot complete on this build, bypass it entirely:

CLI path: hermes update (uses a different, documented update codepath with real PID/file-handle-based lock detection — see [Windows: another hermes.exe is running](https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs/getting-started/updating#windows-another-hermesexe-is-running)), or
Manual reinstall (equivalent to updating to latest main):
powershell
  Remove-Item -Recurse -Force "$env:LOCALAPPDATA\hermes\hermes-agent"
  iex (irm https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/install.ps1)

This only removes the code/venv checkout; config.yaml, .env, skills, and sessions under %LOCALAPPDATA%\hermes (outside the hermes-agent\ subfolder) are preserved.

Both workarounds succeeded where the GUI "Retry update" button consistently failed.

Additional Notes

Related but distinct from [fathah/hermes-desktop#112](https://github.com/fathah/hermes-desktop/issues/112) (Windows Desktop installer wrongly invoking the Unix install.sh via bash) — this issue is about the update path specifically self-locking, not about install method detection.

Happy to provide the full bootstrap-installer.log file or run additional diagnostics if useful.

### Actual Behavior

From %LOCALAPPDATA%\hermes\logs\bootstrap-installer.log, two independent attempts, ~12 minutes apart, each with a different PID, each self-referencing:

Attempt 1 — PID 27204:

2026-07-31T04:28:40.344209Z  INFO hermes_bootstrap_lib: Hermes installer starting mode=Update force_setup=false
2026-07-31T04:28:44.913501Z  INFO bootstrap.log: [update] waiting for Hermes to exit… stage=update
2026-07-31T04:28:44.914523Z  INFO bootstrap.log: [update] updating against branch main stage=update
2026-07-31T04:28:47.453352Z  INFO bootstrap.log: ✗ Another Hermes update is already running (PID 27204, started 7s ago). stage=update
2026-07-31T04:28:47.591373Z  INFO hermes_bootstrap_lib::update: update stage stage=update state=Failed duration_ms=Some(2676) error=Some("Hermes is still running. Close all Hermes windows and try the update again.")

Note: PID 27204 IS this same updater process (hermes-setup.exe, started at 04:28:40). "started 7s ago" = 04:28:47 − 04:28:40, i.e. it is reporting its own start time back to itself.

Attempt 2 (after killing PID 27204, deleting venv\.lock, reopening) — PID 24720:

2026-07-31T04:40:35.686176Z  INFO bootstrap.log: [update] waiting for Hermes to exit… stage=update

items.title: [Bug]: `/background` (`/bg`, `/btw`) is queued until the active CLI turn finishes

labels.name: comp/cli
labels.description: CLI entry point, hermes_cli/, setup wizard

items.body:
## Bug Description

In the classic Hermes CLI/TUI, `/background` and its aliases `/bg` and `/btw` do not start a background task immediately when the foreground agent is already running.

Instead, the command is placed into the normal pending-input path and is only processed after the current foreground turn finishes. This defeats the purpose of `/background`: starting independent work while keeping the current session available.

`/steer` previously had the same CLI scheduling problem and was fixed by dispatching it inline while the agent is running. `/background` still appears to use the blocked queue path.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Start Hermes in the classic interactive CLI/TUI.
2. Submit a prompt that keeps the main agent busy for a while, for example a multi-step code investigation or tool-heavy task.
3. While the main turn is still running, enter:

   ```text
   /bg inspect the test failures independently
   ```

   or:

   ```text
   /btw check whether this dependency has breaking changes
   ```

4. Observe that no background task starts while the main turn is active.
5. Wait for the foreground turn to finish.
6. The `/bg` or `/btw` command is then processed and the background task starts.

## Expected Behavior

The command should be handled immediately from the interactive input path:

```text
foreground agent continues running
        +
background task starts immediately in a separate session
```

The active foreground turn should not be interrupted or steered, and the background command should not wait for the turn boundary.

## Actual Behavior

```text
foreground agent is running
    ↓
/bg or /btw enters the pending-input queue
    ↓
CLI processing loop remains blocked in the foreground chat/run
    ↓
foreground turn finishes
    ↓
/background is finally dispatched
```

From the user's perspective, `/bg` and `/btw` appear to do nothing until the main task completes.

## Why This Is Different From `/steer`

- `/steer <instruction>` injects guidance into the currently running main agent after the next tool batch.
- `/background <prompt>` should create an independent background session/task and leave the main agent unchanged.

They have different semantics, but both need an active-turn input path that does not wait behind the foreground `chat()` call.

## Likely Root Cause

The classic CLI input path queues ordinary submitted text through `_pending_input`. The consumer is blocked inside the active `self.chat()`/agent run, so queued slash commands cannot be processed until the run returns.

`/steer` was fixed by adding an active-agent special case that calls `process_command()` inline from the prompt-toolkit Enter handler rather than putting the command into `_pending_input`.

`/background`, `/bg`, and `/btw` do not appear to have an equivalent inline-dispatch branch.

## Proposed Fix

Follow the `/steer` precedent, but preserve `/background` semantics:

1. Detect whether submitted input resolves to the canonical `background` command while `_agent_running` is true.
2. Dispatch `process_command(text)` directly from the UI/application thread instead of adding it to `_pending_input`.
3. Ensure the handler spawns the independent background task/session without interrupting or steering the foreground agent.
4. Keep normal prompt input queued according to the configured busy-input behavior.

A shared helper may be preferable to command-specific conditionals, for example an allowlist of slash commands that are safe to execute inline during an active CLI run.

## Regression Tests

Suggested coverage:

- Start a blocking/mock foreground `chat()` call.
- Submit `/background do work`, `/bg do work`, and `/btw do work` through the interactive Enter-handler path.
- Assert the background command handler runs before the foreground call is released.
- Assert the command is not added to `_pending_input`.
- Assert the foreground agent is neither interrupted nor given a steer message.
- Assert ordinary user input still follows the configured busy-input behavior.

## Related

- #13354 / PR #13354 — fixed `/steer` being delivered only after the active CLI turn by dispatching it inline.
- #63463 — broader CLI slash-command failures during active subagent waves; related symptom but different reproduction and command semantics.
- #41572 / PR #41578 — gateway-specific handling of `/background`, `/bg`, and `/btw` under busy input modes; not the classic CLI queueing path described here.

## Affected Component

CLI/TUI interactive input dispatch.

## Environment

Observed on current Hermes CLI behavior as of July 31, 2026.

items.title: [Bug]: direct_api_call path for delegated children lacks stale detection — child_timeout kills slow API calls with zero retry (side effect of #72412/#60203)

labels.name: comp/agent
labels.description: Core agent runtime: loop, agent_init, prompt builder, context-compression, responses endpoint

items.body:
## Summary

PR #72412 (fixing #60203) correctly routed delegated children's `chat_completions` API calls through `direct_api_call` to avoid the nested-thread-pool wedge. However, `direct_api_call` has no stale-call detection — unlike `interruptible_api_call` which it replaced for this path. The only timeout protection is the httpx SDK default (read=600s) or `HERMES_API_TIMEOUT` (default 1800s), both of which are **far longer** than the typical `delegation.child_timeout_seconds` (default 240s).

**Result**: when a delegated child's API call hangs mid-request, `child_timeout` fires first, killing the entire child with zero retries — instead of the per-call stale kill + reconnect that `interruptible_api_call` provides.

This is not a regression in the "nested-pool wedge" sense — the wedge fix works. It's a **missing defense-in-depth**: the inline path lost the stale detector that the interrupt-worker path had.

## Evidence

Hermes Agent v0.19.1, macOS, Desktop, `delegation.child_timeout_seconds: 240`.

Subagent (delegate_task child, `glm-5.2` / `zai`, `api_mode=chat_completions`) worked normally for 2 API calls + 2 read_file calls (~16s total), then API call #3 hung:

```
12:39:37 API call #2 completed (3.3s) → read_file completed
          ↓ API call #3 sent
          ... 120s of complete silence (no stale_kill, no TTFB, no event-idle warning) ...
12:41:37 (with local workaround: request_timeout_seconds=120) APITimeoutError → retry
          (without workaround: would hang until child_timeout at 12:43:20)
```

**Without the local workaround** (`request_timeout_seconds` not configured), the timeline is:

```
12:21:11 API call #1 completed (3.4s) → read_file completed
          ↓ API call #2 sent
          ... 3m 56s of complete silence ...
12:25:07 child_timeout 240s → entire child killed, reason=interrupted_during_api_call
```

**Same model in foreground** (interactive turn, not delegated) never hangs — because foreground calls go through `interruptible_api_call` which has stale detection + retry.

## Root Cause

`should_use_direct_api_call` returns `True` for delegated children (`platform=subagent` or `is_delegated_child_context()`). `direct_api_call` runs the request inline with only `_active_request_abort` (for external interrupts) and the httpx timeout as protection. There is no polling loop checking elapsed time vs a stale threshold.

The commit message for #72412 states:

> "the per-request OpenAI client's own httpx timeout (provider `request_timeout_seconds` / `HERMES_API_TIMEOUT`) bounds a genuinely hung provider — the same bound interactive calls already rely on"

This holds for foreground calls (no `child_timeout`), but **not** for delegated children where `child_timeout_seconds` (240s) is much shorter than the httpx default (600–1800s). The httpx timeout never gets a chance to fire.

## Why #72227 stall detection doesn't cover this

The progress-based stall monitor (#72227) has thresholds of **450s idle / 1200s in-tool** — both exceed the default `child_timeout_seconds` of 240s. It was designed for `background=true` detached delegations without a wall-clock child cap, not for sync delegations where `child_timeout` kills first.

## Impact

- Affects **all `chat_completions` providers** (zai, deepseek, xai-oauth, xiaomi, OpenRouter, etc.) when used as delegated children
- Does NOT affect `codex_responses` (stays on `interruptible_api_call`) or `anthropic_messages`
- Any intermittent provider slowness/hang that would normally trigger a stale-kill + retry in foreground mode instead kills the entire child in delegation mode

## Suggested Fix Options

**Option A (minimal, config-level)**: Document that users should set `request_timeout_seconds` on all providers used in delegation, with values < `child_timeout_seconds`. This works but is a footgun — the default behavior is broken.

**Option B (source fix)**: Add a lightweight stale watchdog to `direct_api_call` — a background timer that calls `_abort_active_request("stale_call_kill")` after `_stale_timeout` seconds, mirroring what `interruptible_api_call`'s poll loop does. The infrastructure (`_active_request_abort`, `_compute_non_stream_stale_timeout`) already exists in `direct_api_call` — only the timer is missing.

## Workaround

Set `providers.<id>.request_timeout_seconds` to a value less than `child_timeout_seconds` for each provider used in delegation. E.g., 120s for a 240s child timeout. This makes httpx throw `APITimeoutError` before `child_timeout` fires, triggering the retry loop.

items.title: Curator rollback reports "state restored" after a partial extract but nests the user's skill inside itself

labels.name: comp/agent
labels.description: Core agent runtime: loop, agent_init, prompt builder, context-compression, responses endpoint

items.body:
### What happens

If `hermes curator rollback` fails part-way through extracting the snapshot, the recovery path reports `snapshot extract failed (state restored)` but the skills tree is not restored. The user's own skill directory ends up nested one level inside itself, with the snapshot's partial content sitting where the skill used to be.

### Why

`agent/curator_backup.py:rollback()` stages the current tree, extracts the snapshot into `skills/`, and on failure moves the staged entries back:

```python
except (OSError, tarfile.TarError) as e:
    # Best-effort recover: move staged contents back
    for orig, dest in moved:
        try:
            shutil.move(str(dest), str(orig))
        except OSError:
            pass
    ...
    return (False, f"snapshot extract failed (state restored): {e}", None)
```

`shutil.move` moves *into* an existing destination directory rather than replacing it. Staging leaves `skills/` empty, so this is correct when the extract fails before writing anything. But once the extract has created `skills/alpha/`, the move puts the staged copy at `skills/alpha/alpha/`.

```
$ python3 -c "
import shutil, tempfile
from pathlib import Path
d = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp())
(d/'staged'/'foo').mkdir(parents=True); (d/'staged'/'foo'/'orig.txt').write_text('user data')
(d/'skills'/'foo').mkdir(parents=True); (d/'skills'/'foo'/'partial.txt').write_text('half-extracted')
shutil.move(str(d/'staged'/'foo'), str(d/'skills'/'foo'))
for p in sorted((d/'skills').rglob('*')): print(p.relative_to(d))
"
skills/foo
skills/foo/foo
skills/foo/foo/orig.txt
skills/foo/partial.txt
```

Two further consequences:

- Entries the extract created that the original tree never had are left behind, so the "restored" tree is the user's skills plus a slice of the snapshot.
- The staging dir is removed unconditionally afterwards, so if a move fails the staged copy is deleted too.

### Reproduction

Against `main`:

```python
def extractall(self, path, *args, **kwargs):
    # write part of the archive, then fail like a full disk
    partial = Path(path) / "alpha"
    partial.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    (partial / "SKILL.md").write_text("half written")
    raise OSError(28, "No space left on device")
```

With that patched over the rollback's `tarfile.open`, `skills/alpha/alpha/` exists afterwards and `skills/alpha/SKILL.md` holds the half-written snapshot copy, while `rollback()` returns `(False, "snapshot extract failed (state restored): ...")`.

### Impact

The tree still looks populated, so there is no obvious signal that anything went wrong, and the failure message says the state was restored. The pre-rollback safety snapshot is still on disk, so the data is recoverable, but only by someone who knows to go looking.

### Expected

A failed extract leaves `skills/` exactly as it was found, or says plainly which entries it could not restore and where the staged copies were kept.

items.title: Yuanbao forwarded-records parse never sends its loading heartbeat (coroutine created but not awaited)

labels.name: duplicate
labels.description: This issue or pull request already exists

items.body:
### What happens

On the Yuanbao adapter, forwarding a batch of records to the bot never shows the loading bubble. The user sees no acknowledgement at all while the deep parse runs, which is the slowest part of the inbound path.

Running with warnings visible also produces:

```
RuntimeWarning: coroutine 'ForwardedRecordsParseMiddleware._send_loading_heartbeat' was never awaited
```

### Why

`gateway/platforms/yuanbao.py:2163`, in `ForwardedRecordsParseMiddleware.handle()`:

```python
async def handle(self, ctx: InboundContext, next_fn) -> None:
    try:
        if ctx.forwarded_records:
            self._send_loading_heartbeat(ctx)
            ctx.raw_text = self.build_forward_text(...)
```

`_send_loading_heartbeat` is declared `async` at line 2177:

```python
@staticmethod
async def _send_loading_heartbeat(ctx: InboundContext) -> None:
    """Best-effort RUNNING heartbeat so the user sees a loading bubble."""
    try:
        await ctx.adapter._outbound.heartbeat.send_heartbeat_once(
            ctx.chat_id, WS_HEARTBEAT_RUNNING,
        )
    except Exception:
        pass
```

Calling it without `await` constructs a coroutine object and discards it. `send_heartbeat_once` never runs.

The static binding is fine, since it is a `staticmethod`, so this is only the missing `await`.

### Impact

Cosmetic rather than destructive, but it defeats the one piece of feedback this path was built to provide, and it is the path where the wait is longest. It also leaves an unawaited coroutine behind on every forwarded message.

### Expected

The heartbeat is sent before the deep parse begins.

items.title: `!always` on destructive-slash confirm reports success even when the config write failed

labels.name: comp/cli
labels.description: CLI entry point, hermes_cli/, setup wizard

labels.name: sweeper:risk-compatibility
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may break existing users, config, migrations, defaults, or upgrades

items.body:
## Summary

Answering **Always Approve** on the `/new`//`/reset`//`/clear`//`/undo`
confirmation calls `save_config_value("approvals.destructive_slash_confirm", False)`
and then unconditionally appends:

> ℹ️ Future /clear, /new, /reset, and /undo will run without confirmation.

But the persist can fail, and when it does the user is told it succeeded —
every single time. Two stacked defects:

1. `save_config_value()` (`cli.py`) catches all exceptions and **returns
   `False`** instead of raising. So the `try/except` in the caller's
   `_on_confirm` (`gateway/run.py`) can never observe the failure.
2. `_on_confirm` **ignores the return value** and appends the success note
   regardless. It even carries a comment asserting "The persist itself
   already happened above" — which is exactly the unchecked assumption.

The only trace is a log line the user never sees:

```
ERROR cli: Failed to save config: [Errno 30] Read-only file system: '/Users/hermes/.hermes/config.yaml'
```

## Repro

Any deployment where `HERMES_HOME/config.yaml` isn't writable. The docs' own
Matrix E2EE proxy container is a natural case (config bind-mounted read-only).
Send `/new`, answer `!always`, restart the gateway, send `/new` again → the
confirmation prompt is back, despite the success message.

Even on a writable single-file bind mount this write can't stick:
`atomic_roundtrip_yaml_update` replaces the file (new inode), and container
recreation restores the original.

## Suggested fix

- `_on_confirm` checks `save_config_value()`'s return; on `False`, run the
  action (the user did approve this once) but say so honestly, e.g.:
  "⚠️ Couldn't persist the preference (config not writable) — I'll ask again
  next time. To silence permanently, set
  `approvals.destructive_slash_confirm: false` in config.yaml."
- Optionally: `save_config_value()` grows a `raise`/logging contract so other
  call sites (there are several) can't repeat the pattern.

Workaround for container users meanwhile: set the key declaratively in the
mounted config.

## Notes

- Verified still present on `main` @ dbe14424e (v0.19.1) — byte-identical
  handler.

# Bug: TUI scroll position jumps to middle of conversation after typing input

## Description

When `tui_auto_resume_recent` is enabled and a long conversation is resumed, the TUI scroll position jumps to the **middle of the conversation** after the user sends a message. The expected behavior is that the viewport should follow the newly appended message at the bottom (sticky mode).

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Enable `tui_auto_resume_recent: true` in config
2. Start `hermes --tui` — it resumes a long conversation with many turns
3. Verify the view starts near the bottom (sticky mode active)
4. Type a message and press Enter
5. **Bug**: The view jumps to the middle of the conversation instead of following the new message

## Expected Behavior

After sending a message, the viewport should auto-scroll to the bottom where the new message was appended, maintaining sticky-follow behavior.

## Actual Behavior

The viewport jumps to the middle of the conversation history. The user must manually scroll down or press End to reach the latest message.

## Root Cause Analysis

The issue appears to be in the interaction between:

1. **`useVirtualHistory.ts`** — The virtual scrolling system recalculates the visible item range (`effStart`/`effEnd`) when new items are appended via `appendMessage`. During this recalculation, the `sticky` state or the scroll position may be temporarily inconsistent, causing the viewport to render a middle range.

2. **`useMainApp.ts:303-304`** — `appendMessage` calls `capHistory + appendTranscriptMessage`, which mutates `historyItems` and triggers a re-render of the virtual scroll.

3. **`sticky` state** — Controlled by `useVirtualHistory` via `getLastManualScrollAt()` with a 1200ms debounce window. If the recalculation happens within this window after a user interaction, sticky may be false, and `liveTailActive` controls whether the tail items are mounted.

## Environment

- Hermes Agent v2026.5.7
- TUI mode (`hermes --tui`)
- Platform: WSL (MyUbuntu on Windows)
- Config: `tui_auto_resume_recent: true`

## Related Issues

- #37987 — fix(tui): phantom scroll-jump during streaming
- #74742 — fix(ui-tui): prevent stickyScroll re-activation after manual scroll-up
- #55594 — TUI: Long assistant responses become unreachable (virtual scroll clamp + sticky interaction)
- #54587 — TUI transcript partially blanks when resuming long sessions (mounted range too narrow)

## Workaround

- Press **End** key or **Page Down** to manually scroll back to bottom
- Or use `/redraw` to force a full re-render

items.title: [Bug]: SessionDB retains WAL readers from finished worker threads until shutdown, exhausting RLIMIT_NOFILE

labels.name: comp/agent

labels.name: P1

labels.name: sweeper:risk-session-state
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may lose/corrupt/mis-associate session or context state

items.body:
## Bug Description

A long-lived shared `SessionDB` retains one read-only SQLite WAL connection for every worker thread that has ever used the read path.

`_get_read_conn()` caches the connection in `threading.local()`, but also adds it to the strong `_read_conns` set. When a short-lived worker exits, the strong set keeps the connection alive. The set is drained only by `SessionDB.close()`, which may not run for days in a long-lived gateway.

As a result, file-descriptor usage grows with historical worker count rather than current concurrency, eventually causing process-wide `EMFILE` failures.

A typical visible error is:

```text
OSError: [Errno 24] Too many open files:
'<hermes-home>/sessions/.sessions_*.tmp'
```

The session temporary file is the next attempted open, not the leak source.

## Steps to Reproduce

Tested against current `main`:

```text
f3cda0ceb18d8ba7465a6d223098ef0e56c8fee1
```

Using Python 3.11.15 and SQLite 3.53.1 on Linux:

```python
import gc
import os
import threading
from pathlib import Path

import pytest

from hermes_state import SessionDB


def fd_count():
    return len(os.listdir("/proc/self/fd"))


def test_finished_read_threads_do_not_accumulate_fds(tmp_path: Path):
    db = SessionDB(db_path=tmp_path / "state.db")
    if not db._wal_active:
        db.close()
        pytest.skip("requires WAL")

    db.create_session(session_id="fd-repro", source="cli", model="test")
    assert db.get_session("fd-repro") is not None
    baseline = fd_count()
    errors = []

    def read_once():
        try:
            assert db.get_session("fd-repro") is not None
        except BaseException as exc:
            errors.append(exc)

    try:
        for _ in range(80):
            worker = threading.Thread(target=read_once)
            worker.start()
            worker.join(timeout=10)
            assert not worker.is_alive()

        gc.collect()
        assert not errors

        growth = fd_count() - baseline
        assert growth < 12, (
            f"finished readers retained {growth} descriptors"
        )
    finally:
        db.close()
```

Result on current `main`:

```text
AssertionError: finished readers retained 160 descriptors
```

An independently executed exception-path variant retained 80 descriptors across 40 finished threads.

## Expected Behavior

Connections belonging to finished worker threads should be reclaimed during the lifetime of the shared `SessionDB`.

Descriptor usage should be bounded by current reader concurrency, not by the number of historical worker threads.

## Actual Behavior

A long-running gateway reached the following sanitized state:

```text
process soft nofile limit     1024
open descriptors              1024
currently live threads          44
state.db read-only FDs          474
state.db read-write FDs           8
state.db-wal FDs                476
state.db-shm FDs                  1
```

The large difference between 44 live threads and 474 read-only database handles shows that readers belonging to finished threads were retained.

SQLite `quick_check` returned `ok`, `foreign_key_check` returned no rows, and the host-wide file table was healthy.

## Affected Component

- Gateway
- Agent Core / `SessionDB`
- SQLite WAL read path

The issue is platform-independent, although the reproducer uses Linux `/proc` for exact descriptor counting.

## Environment / Debug Report

- Hermes Agent: 0.19.0
- Reproduced on current `main`: `f3cda0ceb`
- Python: 3.11.15
- SQLite: 3.53.1
- OS: Linux

## Root Cause Analysis

Current `main`:

1. `SessionDB.__init__()` creates `_read_local` and a strong `_read_conns` set.
2. `_get_read_conn()` creates one read-only connection per thread.
3. Each connection is cached in thread-local state and added to `_read_conns`.
4. A worker can finish, but `_read_conns` keeps its connection strongly reachable.
5. There is no runtime reaping of connections whose owner thread has exited.
6. `_read_conns` is drained only by `SessionDB.close()`.

The unbounded retention was introduced when tracked readers were added in `f228e145ba35cbbf785eded2021ae6682285b91b`.

A WAL reader commonly accounts for both a `state.db` and `state.db-wal` descriptor, matching the approximately two descriptors retained per worker in the reproducer.

## Relationship to #74304

#74304 is related and complementary, but it does not cover this lifecycle stage.

It adds `check_same_thread=False` so `SessionDB.close()` can drain connections created by finished workers from another thread. That fixes final shutdown cleanup.

This issue occurs before shutdown: the shared `SessionDB` remains alive while historical worker connections accumulate. The reproducer measures descriptor growth before `db.close()`, so #74304 alone does not change the result.

## Proposed Fix Requirements

The final implementation should:

- preserve same-thread connection reuse and read-path independence from the writer lock;
- preserve per-thread open-failure memoization;
- associate cached readers with their owner thread;
- reclaim readers whose owner has finished and which are not actively leased;
- prevent new readers from opening after `SessionDB.close()` begins;
- avoid closing an in-flight reader from another thread;
- keep descriptor growth bounded under many short-lived workers.

An owner-aware reaper combined with `check_same_thread=False` is one possible minimal implementation. A bounded reusable reader pool is another option.

Opening and closing a connection for every `_read_ctx()` prevents the unbounded leak, but local benchmarks showed roughly 20x overhead for `get_session()` and 10x for `search_messages()`, so it does not appear suitable as the final performance-preserving fix.

## Contribution

I am willing to prepare a focused PR and coordinate it with #74304.

### What happens

Python keeps only the last definition of a name in a scope, so a duplicate silently deletes the first. There is no error, no warning, and no skip. Four have accumulated in the test tree, and two of them cost real coverage.

### 1. An autouse fixture was replaced for a whole module

`tests/agent/test_auxiliary_client.py` defines `_clean_env` twice at module level, at line 63 and again at line 3459. Both are `@pytest.fixture(autouse=True)`, so the second one governs all 158 tests in the file.

The original:

```python
for key in (
    "OPENROUTER_API_KEY", "OPENAI_BASE_URL", "OPENAI_API_KEY",
    "OPENAI_MODEL", "LLM_MODEL", "NOUS_INFERENCE_BASE_URL",
    "ANTHROPIC_API_KEY", "ANTHROPIC_TOKEN", "CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN",
):
    monkeypatch.delenv(key, raising=False)
import agent.auxiliary_client as _aux_mod
_aux_mod._aux_unhealthy_until.clear()
_aux_mod._aux_unhealthy_logged_at.clear()
yield
_aux_mod._aux_unhealthy_until.clear()
_aux_mod._aux_unhealthy_logged_at.clear()
```

The one that actually runs, added alongside the NVIDIA billing-header feature in `13c3d4b4e`:

```python
for key in (
    "OPENROUTER_API_KEY", "OPENAI_BASE_URL", "OPENAI_API_KEY",
    "NVIDIA_API_KEY", "NVIDIA_BASE_URL",
):
    monkeypatch.delenv(key, raising=False)
```

So the module lost, for every test in it:

- env isolation for `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, `ANTHROPIC_TOKEN`, `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN`, `OPENAI_MODEL`, `LLM_MODEL`, `NOUS_INFERENCE_BASE_URL`
- the `_aux_unhealthy_until` / `_aux_unhealthy_logged_at` reset around each test

The second loss left tracks. Two tests clear that cache by hand, and one says why:

```python
pollutes the module-level ``_aux_unhealthy_until`` dict (10-min TTL)
```

The first loss is the same class as #75230: a unit test reading the developer's real credentials out of the environment.

### 2. A Mattermost test never ran

`tests/gateway/test_mattermost.py` has two copies of `test_progress_send_with_invalid_thread_root_never_falls_back_flat`, at lines 199 and 247. The surviving copy omits the state the name is about:

```python
 self.adapter._api_get = AsyncMock(return_value={"id": "bad_root", "root_id": ""})
-self.adapter._last_post_status = 400
-self.adapter._last_post_error = "api.context.invalid_param.app_error: invalid root_id"
 self.adapter._api_post = AsyncMock(return_value={})
```

The case the test name describes, a recorded 400 `invalid root_id`, is never exercised.

### 3 and 4. Harmless, but they hid the pattern

`tests/gateway/test_tts_media_routing.py` has two byte-identical copies of `test_non_streaming_media_failure_notifies_user`. `tests/agent/test_credential_pool.py` defines `_codex_auth_store` twice with different shapes; neither is called by anything.

### Expected

A duplicate definition in a test module is a mistake every time. It should be impossible to land one without CI saying so.

items.title: [Bug]: Tauri updater handoff fails on macOS — HERMES_UPDATE_HANDOFF_PID mismatch causes perpetual update failure

labels.name: sweeper:risk-compatibility
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may break existing users, config, migrations, defaults, or upgrades

items.body:
## Bug Description

On macOS, the Tauri-based updater (`hermes-setup --update`) always fails with "Hermes is still running" because the `HERMES_UPDATE_HANDOFF_PID` handoff mechanism between the Rust updater and the Python `hermes update` child process is broken.

The Rust updater writes the `.hermes-update-in-progress` marker with its own PID, then spawns `hermes update` with `HERMES_UPDATE_HANDOFF_PID` set to its PID. The Python child reads the marker, but the PID check fails — it refuses to proceed and exits with code 2 (`UPDATE_EXIT_CONCURRENT`). The Rust updater catches exit code 2 and shows "Hermes is still running. Close all Hermes windows and try the update again."

**This makes ALL in-app updates on macOS permanently broken** — every attempt fails within ~200ms without ever reaching the actual update logic.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Open Hermes Desktop on macOS
2. Click "Update" when prompted
3. The update window immediately shows: "Hermes is still running. Close all Hermes windows and try the update again."
4. Close all Hermes windows
5. Click "Retry update" — same error
6. Repeat forever — update never succeeds

## Expected Behavior

The Tauri updater should successfully hand off to `hermes update` via the `HERMES_UPDATE_HANDOFF_PID` mechanism, and the update should proceed.

## Actual Behavior

Every update attempt fails in ~200ms with "Hermes is still running" without ever reaching the git pull / dependency install stages.

## Root Cause Analysis

### The Handoff Mechanism (update.rs + update_lock.py)

1. **Desktop Electron** pre-writes `.hermes-update-in-progress` with the Tauri updater PID (`writeUpdateMarker()`)
2. **Tauri updater** (`UpdateMarkerGuard::acquire()`) reads the marker, sees its own PID → treats as non-ownership → overwrites with its own PID
3. **Tauri updater** sets `HERMES_UPDATE_HANDOFF_PID` env var to its PID (`update_child_env()` at line 918-921)
4. **Tauri updater** spawns Python `hermes update` child via `run_streamed()`
5. **Python `hermes update`** (`UpdateLock.acquire()` in `update_lock.py`) reads the marker → finds a live PID → checks `HANDOFF_PID_ENV` → **mismatch** → refuses to acquire → exits with code 2

The bug: the Python child does NOT receive (or correctly match) the `HERMES_UPDATE_HANDOFF_PID` value, so it treats the Tauri updater's marker as a foreign lock and refuses.

### Log Evidence

```
2026-07-30T15:00:15.066886Z  INFO bootstrap.log: [update] waiting for Hermes to exit… stage=update
2026-07-30T15:00:15.066955Z  INFO bootstrap.log: [update] updating against branch main stage=update
2026-07-30T15:00:15.229303Z  INFO bootstrap.log: ✗ Another Hermes update is already running (PID 41934, started 1s ago). stage=update
2026-07-30T15:00:15.263739Z  INFO hermes_bootstrap_lib::update: update stage stage=update state=Failed duration_ms=Some(196) error=Some("Hermes is still running. Close all Hermes windows and try the update again.")
```

Key observations:
- Update fails in **196ms** — never reaches git pull / dependency install
- PID 41934 is the Tauri updater's own PID, not a foreign process
- The "started 1s ago" suggests the marker was written by the same updater instance
- **Every single attempt** from July 30 15:00 onward fails identically
- The marker file `.hermes-update-in-progress` is properly cleaned up by `UpdateMarkerGuard::Drop` between attempts, so the issue is NOT a stale marker — it is a handoff mismatch during the attempt

### Code References

- `apps/bootstrap-installer/src-tauri/src/update.rs:918-921` — sets `HERMES_UPDATE_HANDOFF_PID`
- `hermes_cli/update_lock.py:114-127` — reads `HANDOFF_PID_ENV`
- `hermes_cli/update_lock.py:202-215` — `acquire()` checks PID match
- `apps/desktop/electron/update-marker.ts:128-138` — `writeUpdateMarker()`

### Workaround

Run update from terminal (bypasses Tauri updater entirely):

```bash
/Users/xialinhan/.hermes/hermes-agent/venv/bin/hermes update --yes --branch main
```

This succeeds because the Python CLI update path does not use the Tauri handoff mechanism.

## Affected Component

Desktop App (Tauri updater + Python update lock handoff)

## Operating System

macOS (Darwin 25.5.0, Sequoia)

## Hermes Version

Hermes Agent v0.18.2 (before manual update)

## Additional Context

This appears to be the same root cause as:
- #74531 — "In-app update stuck in another update loop"
- #74942 — "Desktop app updater detects itself as another instance"
- #74836 — "macOS in-app update permanently broken"

All three report the same symptom: the updater detects a "foreign" PID that is actually its own or its child's PID.

## Are you willing to submit a PR for this?

- [ ] I'd like to fix this myself and submit a PR

items.body:
## Description

When a background skill-save turn errors out (e.g. relay scope corruption), the session lock is never released. This causes a **permanent gateway deadlock** until manual process restart.

## Reproduction

1. Hermes Agent gateway running with Telegram polling
2. A session completes its main response but spawns a background skill-update turn (auto-skill-save with a different model)
3. The background turn errors (e.g. `skill_manage` blocked by security scan → relay scope corruption)
4. Session never closes → `_active_sessions[session_key]` stays held
5. PTB updater stops
6. No new inbound messages possible → `_heal_stale_session_lock()` never fires (it only triggers on inbound message at `gateway/platforms/base.py:5565`)
7. Gateway remains alive but completely silent — no new Telegram messages processed

## Root Cause

There is no proactive mechanism to clean up stale session locks. The existing `_heal_stale_session_lock()` at `gateway/platforms/base.py:5330` only runs **reactively** when a new inbound message arrives. If the updater is dead (no new messages), the heal never fires → circular deadlock.

Additionally, `_start_session_processing()` already attaches `done_callback`s to tasks (line 5384), but they only handle tracking set cleanup — they don't heal the session lock.

## Proposed Fix

Add a `done_callback` in `_start_session_processing()` that automatically heals the session lock when the task exits, regardless of exit reason. With identity verification to avoid cross-contamination:

```python
def _heal_lock_on_done(completed_task, key=session_key):
    if self._session_tasks.get(key) is not completed_task:
        return  # replaced by a newer task
    self._heal_stale_session_lock(key)

task.add_done_callback(_heal_lock_on_done)
```

## Impact

Gateway completely stops responding to Telegram messages (~1x/day on affected instances). Requires manual `systemctl restart` to recover. Users perceive Hermes as "crashed" when the process is actually alive.

## Related

- #73746 — relay scope corruption (the trigger for the background task error)
